transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hello Ms. Williams. I wanted to come in and talk to you about why you had to come back to the emergency department last night.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just don't understand why this is happening. I was told I was fine to go home.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I have the charts here. Looking at the timeline, the post-operative protocol required you to stay for twenty-four hours after the procedure. However, you were discharged six hours earlier than that requirement. Because you left too soon, your wound didn't get the necessary observation time and it started to complicate, which is why you're back here now. Does that make sense so far?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Wait, so you guys just let me leave too early? I can't believe this. I have two kids at home and I'm barely hanging on with two jobs. I can't keep coming back and forth to the hospital.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand that this is frustrating.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Frustrating? I'm terrified. I don't know who is watching my kids right now or if I'm even going to be able to work next week. I thought the surgery was over and I was on the mend. Now I'm back in a hospital gown and I don't even know if I'm actually okay.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is a lot to handle. Do you have any other questions about the timing of the discharge?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just want to know why it happened. Did someone forget? Was I just a number?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The discharge papers were processed before the full observation window had closed. It was a breakdown in the timing of the protocol.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It feels like nobody is actually saying they're sorry. I've lost two days of work already.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The medical team is focused on getting the wound stabilized now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That's not what I asked. I'm sitting here wondering if I can even pick up my children tomorrow and you're talking about stabilization. Do you even realize how much this messes up my life?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know it's a stressful situation.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It's not just stressful, it's a disaster. I'm alone in this.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see you're overwhelmed. Just to be clear on the facts, the error was that the six-hour window was missed. To make sure we're on the same page, can you tell me what your understanding is of why you came back?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Because you guys sent me home too early and my wound opened up or got infected or whatever.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is correct. The wound is not infected, but it did start to separate because we didn't monitor the initial healing phase long enough.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So what happens now? How long am I staying?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll have to see how the wound looks.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What does that mean? Do I have a date? Do I tell my boss I'm out for another week?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will keep an eye on it and someone will probably let you know later on.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Later? I need to coordinate childcare. I can't just wait for someone to maybe tell me something.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll just have to see how things progress.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is unbelievable. I come back because of a mistake and now I can't even get a straight answer on when I can go home to my children.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are monitoring the site.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel like I'm just being pushed around. First I'm pushed out the door too early, and now I'm being told to just wait.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I hear that you're worried about your kids.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes, I am! They're everything. And I'm stuck here because of a mistake that shouldn't have happened. Who is responsible for this?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was a lapse in the discharge process.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That's not an answer. Was it you? Was it the nurse?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The team handled the discharge.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just feel like no one is taking ownership. I'm the one suffering the consequences.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I've explained the error with the protocol.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You've explained the facts, but you haven't actually acknowledged that this was a failure.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The situation is being addressed.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm just so tired. I'm so tired of fighting for basic information.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is there anyone else I can talk to about the plan for my recovery?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We can check back in once the attending doctor makes their rounds.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When is that?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Sometime this morning.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I hope it's soon. I really need to call my babysitter.

H.justification: The resident allows the patient to finish their turns and remains regulated despite significant pushback, with no interruptions or rushing language.

E.justification: The error (discharged six hours early) is named in the first turn, lay language is used, and comprehension is checked ('Does that make sense so far?' and 'can you tell me what your understanding is').

A.justification: No direct apology language is used, and responsibility is deflected to 'the protocol', 'the discharge process', and 'the team'.

R.justification: The resident names specific emotions ('frustrating', 'overwhelmed', 'worried about your kids') and references the patient's specific concerns.

T.justification: The resident provides only placeholders and vague responses ('we'll have to see', 'someone will probably let you know later', 'sometime this morning') without a concrete plan or timeline.
